title: Behold, the King of Zion Rides
description: Behold, the King of Zion Rides in Tonic Solfa to MATERNA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Morningland (Paisley, 1911), headed “Palm Sunday”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre Double (8.6.8.6.8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to MATERNA; any other Common Metre Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Be-hold, the King of Zi-on rides, But not in vain ar-ray; The peo-ple wave their good-ly palms, With gar-ments strew the way; And loud ho-san-nas fill the air From crowds that, surg-ing, throng; 'Tis meet to hon-our Him Who rides With cheer, and shout, and song.

lines: Behold, the King of Zion rides,
But not in vain array;
The people wave their goodly palms,
With garments strew the way;
And loud hosannas fill the air
From crowds that, surging, throng;
'Tis meet to honour Him Who rides
With cheer, and shout, and song.
O Zion, of your God beloved,
The day of strife is nigh,
Yet comes He not with armour clad,
And sword upon His thigh;
The weapons of your mighty King
No other hand could wield,
The might of God is in His arm,
The will of God His shield.
See, on the cross, without the wall,
The King Immortal dies;
Not now hosannas fill the air, —
The shouts of hell arise;
But in that hour of triumph, deemed,
Satanic might is slain,
For He Who bows the head in death,
Shall rise to life again.
O Zion, hail your mighty King,
Your palms around Him wave,
And strew your garments in the way
Of Him Who rides to save;
And when He mounts His regal throne,
By bloody conflict won,
Give homage to the King of heaven,
God's One Eternal Son.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Morningland (1911)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Morningland; set to MATERNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
